ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening standards: Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the reporting entity must conduct customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), screen all parties against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the New Zealand designated persons list maintained under the United Nations Act 1946 and the Russia Sanctions Act 2022, and, for all international wire transfers, reasonably apply OFAC, UK Office of Financial Sanctions, and EU consolidated sanctions screening to identify asset-freeze and prohibition risk. The Department of Internal Affairs enforces compliance with the Identity Verification Code of Practice 2013 and requires adoption of a documented risk-based AML/CFT compliance programme.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Companies Register — accessible at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz (under the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Latin-script characters (A-Z) and may include Te Reo Māori words with macrons. Non-Latin scripts, symbols, and pictographic elements are not accepted. The suffix 'Limited' (or 'Tapui Limited' in Te Reo Māori) is mandatory for a limited liability company. The Companies Office applies a similarity test against existing registered names and reserved names, and will reject names that suggest Crown or government sponsorship, offensive or misleading connotations, or are inconsistent with the Companies Act 1993.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Crown', 'Government', 'National', 'Ministry' (unless the relevant department gives written approval)
'Bank', 'Trust', 'Insurance', 'University', 'Polytechnic' (requires prior consent of the applicable regulator or statutory licensing authority)
'Chartered Accountant', 'Law Society', 'Audit' or 'Registered' (professional-body approval required before use)
Offensive, obscene, or names contrary to public policy or that are likely to mislead the public
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar refuses to reserve or register a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the New Zealand Companies Office within 20 working days of the refusal, citing the grounds under ss 21-23 of the Companies Act 1993 and explaining why the name does not contravene the statutory prohibitions. The Registrar may also permit the name if written consent from the relevant authority (e.g., the Reserve Bank, Ministry of Education, or professional body) is provided. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. As a pragmatic alternative, the applicant may immediately file a fresh name reservation for a new name without additional administrative fees. The 20-working-day reservation period is not extendable; if still required after expiry, a new reservation application is necessary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are accepted for the registered office requirement under the Companies Act 1993 only if the address is a genuine physical street address in New Zealand at which legal documents can be served. However, for an ISIC 7810 study-abroad / immigration-visa consultancy, the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007 and the AML/CFT supervisor expect a substantive local commercial presence, client-facing premises, secure physical and digital record-keeping, and at least one New Zealand-based licensed immigration adviser if immigration advice is provided. A virtual-only office will be treated as an elevated money-laundering risk factor and may result in delayed incorporation approval, refusal of an immigration adviser licence application, or heightened AML/CFT inspection frequency.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT Group) or the Immigration Advisers Authority is approximately 10% in the first 12 months, rising to about 25% in year 2 and up to 40% in year 3 for a medium-risk reporting entity handling client escrow funds and visa application processes. The likelihood increases further if suspicious transaction reports are filed or adverse media/negative compliance audit findings appear.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), ss. 12, 15, 16, 88, 89, 107, 151-153, 200; Income Tax Act 2007, s. YD 2 (corporate residence); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007; Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021; Building Act 2004; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ngā Kaporeihana), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Company (statutory application for incorporation) filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 1993 for a company limited by shares; the board determines share consideration. No statutory escrow account is required at incorporation. However, because the business scope is international student placement and golden visa immigration advisory, the Immigration Advisers Code of Conduct and the AML/CFT Act 2009 together require client monies to be held in a designated escrow or trust account, prudentially capitalised at an initial balance of not less than NZ$1,000 (approximately USD 610) as a client protection buffer.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [STUDY FIRST INTERNATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED]

A duly convened meeting of the board of directors (the 'Board') of Study First International Company Limited (the 'Company') was held on [date] at [registered office address], New Zealand. Present: [Director 1] (Chair), [Director 2] (Company Secretary). A quorum being present, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and passed unanimously:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT
RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to section 107 of the Companies Act 1993, the Company shall allot and issue 1,000 Ordinary Shares of NZ$1.00 each (total consideration NZ$1,000) to the subscriber shareholder, fully paid or credited as paid, and that the consideration be deposited into the client escrow account referred to in resolution 4.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION
RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [full street address], Auckland, New Zealand, being a physical address open to service of documents during ordinary business hours, and that notification be given to the Registrar of Companies in accordance with sections 88 and 89 of the Companies Act 1993.

3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS
RESOLVED THAT (a) [Director 1] be and is hereby appointed Managing Director of the Company; (b) [Director 2] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary of the Company; and (c) such officers shall exercise all powers conferred by the Company's Constitution and the Companies Act 1993, including the power to open bank accounts, execute client engagement contracts, and make statutory filings.

4. CLIENT FUNDS ESCROW AND PAYMENT RAILS
RESOLVED THAT the Managing Director be and is hereby authorised to open an escrow account with a New Zealand-registered bank for the receipt of visa and study placement fees, such account to be operated strictly in accordance with the Immigration Advisers Code of Conduct and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and that wire-transfer payments shall be accepted only into such escrow account.

5. STATUTORY FILINGS AND LICENSING
RESOLVED THAT the officers be and are hereby authorised to (a) file all incorporation and annual return documents with the New Zealand Companies Office; (b) apply for an IRD number and appropriate tax status with Inland Revenue; (c) register the Company as an AML/CFT reporting entity with the Department of Internal Affairs; (d) retain and supervise licensed immigration advisers under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007; and (e) register the Company's education placement agency with the New Zealand Qualifications Authority in accordance with the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021.

DATED this [day] day of [month], [year] at [location], New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Registry Clearance Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online Companies Register, www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search of the Companies Register to ensure the proposed name, including the mandatory suffix 'Limited', is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing or reserved name under sections 20 and 21 of the Companies Act 1993. File a name reservation request through the Companies Office online portal, or alternatively await name approval as part of the incorporation application. If the name contains a restricted word (e.g., 'Trust', 'Bank', 'University'), submit a written consent from the relevant oversight body. Confirm the suitability of the name for the immigration and education advisory business in all markets of operation.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and suffix reservation application
Consent letter of the holder of any existing name if similarity is present
Board resolution authorising the selection and use of the proposed name
Consent of the New Zealand Qualifications Authority if the name contains educational terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar of Companies refuses registration of the name on grounds of misleading similarity, file a written reconsideration request under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 within 20 working days, attaching trademark registrations, explanatory evidence, or written consent of the objecting party. Alternatively, incorporate under an approved name and subsequently apply for a change of name under section 33 of the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitution and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel admitted in New Zealand and a notary public for certification of foreign shareholder documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct New Zealand-qualified counsel to draft a company constitution under section 55 of the Companies Act 1993, tailored to the tax-exempt international company structure, permitting non-resident directors and shareholders, providing for maintenance of a client escrow account, and specifying board authorities. Prepare the share subscription agreement whereby the sole subscriber agrees to take 1,000 Ordinary Shares of NZ$1.00 each. Execute all documents in counterpart, have foreign shareholder and director identity documents notarised and apostilled, and obtain each director's signed consent to act in the prescribed Companies Office form.
required_dossiers: Draft company constitution (s. 55, Companies Act 1993)
Share subscription and allotment agreement
Prescribed consent-to-act forms of each director (Companies Office form)
Certified passport copies and proof of address of each director and shareholder
Notarised power of attorney appointing a local registered agent, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office or counsel identifies that the constitution conflicts with the Companies Act 1993 or the AML/CFT Act 2009, adopt a special resolution amending the constitution under section 117 of the Companies Act 1993 and re-file the amended instrument. If a director's consent is ineffective, obtain a fresh signed consent and submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registry Services Division, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the electronic Form 2 'Application for Registration of a Company' via the Companies Register portal, providing the approved company name, the physical registered office address in New Zealand, the postal address, the shareholding structure, and the particulars of at least one natural person director who must be at least 18 years old. Upload the executed constitution and all director and shareholder consents. Pay the statutory filing fee of NZ$105.70 (approximately USD 65) by approved debit or credit card. Upon successful processing, the system issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation and a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Completed online Form 2 incorporating the company
Executed company constitution (uploaded)
Prescribed consent forms of each director
Evidence of the physical registered office address (lease or letter of consent from landlord)
Record of payment of the statutory filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the Companies Office issue a requisition notice identifying defects in the application, the applicant shall have 20 working days from the notice date to file an amended Form 2 or additional documents through the portal. If the Registrar declines registration, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Senior Courts Act 2016 or submit a fresh application after curing the identified deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: New Zealand Business Number Activation and Inland Revenue Tax Status Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (Te Tari Taake); New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register integrated with the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the NZBN automatically issued with the Certificate of Incorporation and use it to complete the Inland Revenue department registration. Submit Form IR596 to obtain a New Zealand IRD number. Because the entity is classified as a tax-exempt international company with offshore management, file a place-of-effective-management (POEM) declaration and any required non-resident or exempt status election under the Income Tax Act 2007. If the company will make supplies exceeding NZ$60,000 in a 12-month period, register for goods and services tax; otherwise apply for an exemption or remain unregistered for GST. Retain all registration confirmations in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number
IR596 application for an IRD number
Place of effective management (POEM) declaration
Board resolution confirming offshore management and tax-exempt operations
First-year financial projections for the immigration advisory business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue disputes the POEM declaration and asserts that the company is a New Zealand tax resident due to management exercised in New Zealand, the company shall respond with a detailed operational narrative, a directors' meeting diary, and evidence that client contracts are executed offshore. If the dispute persists, file a Notice of Proposed Adjustment under the Tax Administration Act 1994, seek a binding ruling, and engage a licensed tax agent to expedite resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration and Client Escrow Account Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) - Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Supervision; registered commercial bank in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a reporting entity under section 130 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 through the DIA online registration portal, because the business uses wire transfers and escrow account payment rails for client visa and study placement fees. Prepare and submit the AML/CFT compliance programme and an entity-level risk assessment, appoint a designated compliance officer, and establish a customer due diligence framework covering beneficial ownership, source of funds, and enhanced vetting of high-net-worth 'golden visa' applicants who are politically exposed persons. Open a segregated client escrow account with a registered New Zealand bank, execute the bank's escrow mandate, and record the escrow arrangement in the company's compliance manual.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT compliance programme and written risk assessment
Appointment letter of the designated AML/CFT compliance officer
Beneficial ownership and control structure chart
Escrow account application and bank mandate
Client identity verification and ongoing monitoring policies
Information security and data protection policy for client passport and visa data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIA issues a direction to comply or suspends the reporting entity registration, the company shall submit a corrective action plan within 30 days, remediate gaps in the compliance programme, and provide evidence of staff training. If the DIA imposes pecuniary penalties or an unfavourable determination, the company may seek review by the Financial Markets Authority appellate panel and, thereafter, appeal to the High Court of New Zealand on a question of law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Immigration Adviser Licensing and Supervision Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Immigration Advisers Authority (IAA), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each natural person providing immigration advice, submit a complete application for a Full Immigration Adviser Licence under section 36 of the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007. The applicant must hold the approved qualification, namely the Graduate Diploma in New Zealand Immigration Advice (Level 6) or an equivalent recognised credential, and must pass the IAA's Knowledge and Skills examination. The application must include a certificate of professional indemnity insurance with cover of at least NZ$100,000 per claim, two character references, and a clean New Zealand police certificate. Following approval, the company must maintain a register of licensed advisers, ensure that no unlicensed person provides immigration advice, and comply with the Immigration Advisers Code of Conduct regarding client funds, fee transparency, and conflicts of interest. For golden visa (Active Investor Plus) advice, the licensed adviser must maintain current knowledge of Immigration New Zealand investor and residence policy.
required_dossiers: Immigration Adviser Licensing application form (IAA prescribed form)
Graduate Diploma in New Zealand Immigration Advice certificate or recognised equivalent
Knowledge and Skills examination result
Professional indemnity insurance certificate (minimum NZ$100,000 per claim)
New Zealand police certificate and two character references
Employment contract of the licensed immigration adviser
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IAA declines a licence application, the applicant may request an internal reconsideration within 5 working days, providing supplementary evidence of qualifications or insurance. The decision may be appealed to the Immigration Advisers Complaints and Disciplinary Tribunal (IACDT) under section 74 of the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007 within 20 working days of the decision. A fresh application may be submitted once all statutory deficiencies have been cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Education Placement Agency Registration and Civil Defence / Workplace Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA) - Code of Practice Compliance Section; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); territorial authority issuing the Building Warrant of Fitness; WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a recognised education placement agency with NZQA by executing the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021 acknowledgement and entering into agency agreements with NZQA-approved education providers. For physical premises, ensure compliance with the Building Act 2004 by maintaining an up-to-date building warrant of fitness for the office fit-out, submit a fire evacuation scheme to Fire and Emergency New Zealand if required by the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, and conduct a workplace health and safety self-audit under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, recording the risk register and staff training records. The company shall also implement secure handling procedures for client immigration files in accordance with the Privacy Act 2020 obligations applicable to visa application data.
required_dossiers: Signed acknowledgement of the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021
Agency agreement with at least one NZQA-registered education provider
Lease agreement for the New Zealand office premises
Building warrant of fitness or the territorial authority application for same
Fire evacuation scheme plan and certificate, if applicable
Health and Safety at Work policy, risk register, and staff training records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NZQA finds a breach of the Code of Practice, the company shall submit a corrective action plan within 10 working days and implement agreed remediation steps. A compliance order issued by Fire and Emergency New Zealand may be remedied by submitting a revised evacuation scheme or undertaking drills, and any decision may be appealed to the District Court under section 104 of the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. Improvement or prohibition notices issued by WorkSafe shall be cured by obtaining a relevant compliance certificate, completing staff training, and confirming the risk register is current.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Immigration Advisers Authority (IAA) within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA) for education placement agency compliance; Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) for AML/CFT supervision; local territorial authority for building compliance; Fire and Emergency New Zealand; WorkSafe New Zealand
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Immigration Adviser Full Licence under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007; Registered International Student Placement Agency under the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021; AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, in coordination with the local territorial authority underthe Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based professional services business with no industrial process, no manufacturing discharge, and no significant land disturbance. Under the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004 and the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Sources of Human Drinking Water) Regulations 2007, the activity is classified as low-risk commercial office use, requiring only a permitted baseline assessment for the office premises and no full EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Nil manufacturing emissions; the company shall comply with the local council trade waste and wastewater discharge provisions for office sanitary facilities, the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 obligations for office recycling and e-waste disposal, and the Ministry for the Environment's national solid waste guidelines, remaining below the 1,000 tonnes per year waste declaration threshold. For any office fit-out, compliance with New Zealand Building Code clauses E1 (protection from fire) and G5 (interior environment) is required, with appropriate air quality ventilation certification for meeting rooms occupied by clients.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification through an approved fire evacuation scheme filed with Fire and Emergency New Zealand under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; structural and building systems clearance through a Building Warrant of Fitness issued by the relevant territorial authority under the Building Act 2004; workplace health and safety clearance through a WorkSafe New Zealand self-audited compliance statement under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; and secure client-file handling clearance verified by the Department of Internal Affairs in respect of the AML/CFT reporting entity registration, covering the physical and digital storage of immigration and golden visa client records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand, headquartered at 55 Featherston Street, Wellington; e-services portal myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz. Company incorporation, NZBN issuance, and annual return filing are administered by the New Zealand Companies Office (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz), which transmits registration data to Inland Revenue.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — NZ-incorporated entity: incorporate online via the Companies Office electronic register; an Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number and a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) are issued automatically upon registration. Step 2 — Non-resident or foreign-incorporated entity: submit Form IR742 (Application for IRD Number for a Non-Resident Company) to Inland Revenue, attaching certified certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, the shareholders and directors register, and a statement of New Zealand-source activities; lodgement may be effected electronically through myIR or by a New Zealand tax agent. Step 3 — GST registration: file Form IR356 or apply via myIR, nominating the filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly); non-resident suppliers of remote services use the myIR non-resident registration path and may register with a non-resident business address. Step 4 — The statutory IRD number is an 8-9 digit identifier (format nnn-nnn-nnn) and must be quoted on all tax invoices, GST returns, customs export declarations, and income tax filings; the full procurement timeline is 1-5 business days for the IRD number and immediate issuance of the NZBN upon incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — The CK_IC International Company is a limited-liability company assigned the Tax-Exempt-Zone profile. Under the territorial operation of the Income Tax Act 2007, income derived from offshore sources (international student placement fees and golden visa residence advisory fees invoiced to non-resident clients located outside New Zealand) is not chargeable to New Zealand income tax where the company is not a New Zealand tax resident (i.e., control and management is exercised offshore, or a double-tax-agreement tie-breaker deems it resident in another jurisdiction) or, if resident, where the income is exempt foreign-sourced income. New Zealand-source income — including commissions invoiced to New Zealand educational institutions and fees from clients physically present in New Zealand — remains within the New Zealand tax net and is taxed at the corporate rate of 28% unless the Look-Through Company election applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections under New Zealand law: (i) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, allowing income, expenditure, and tax credits to flow through to shareholders (available to companies with five or fewer qualifying New Zealand-resident shareholder individuals or trustees); (ii) treaty non-resident election: where a double-tax-agreement tie-breaker determines residency in another state, the company may be treated as a non-resident for New Zealand tax purposes; (iii) grey-list and active-business exemptions under the Controlled Foreign Company rules (subparts CQ and EX) to prevent attribution of foreign income where the CK_IC holds offshore subsidiaries; (iv) hybrid and branch mismatch ordering elections under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018; (v) GST statutory elections: voluntary GST registration for non-resident suppliers, the going-concern zero-rating election under section 11(1)(m) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, and the export-evidence election under section 11A(4) permitting zero-rating of exported services where the supplier holds the prescribed non-resident evidence.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a value-added tax levied under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, administered by the Inland Revenue Department; supplemented by the GST on Remote Services (cross-border business-to-consumer services) regime effective 1 October 2016.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period. The threshold applies to a person carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand and to a non-resident supplier of remote services (including online advisory, education placement, and immigration consulting) to New Zealand-resident consumers, measured by the value of supplies made to New Zealand consumers. Once the threshold is exceeded, or where there is a reasonable expectation that it will be exceeded in the next 12 months, registration is compulsory and must be applied for within 21 days of the end of the month in which the threshold was crossed. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold, including for non-residents wishing to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, pre-clearance API reporting, or digital stamping of invoices. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the Peppol PINT interoperability framework via accredited New Zealand access points; the Inland Revenue Department myIR system accepts standard GST returns (Form GST101) and does not perform per-invoice fiscal validation. Statutory tax-invoice rules apply: a standard tax invoice must be issued within 28 days of the time of supply for taxable supplies exceeding NZD 50 (GST-inclusive); a simplified tax invoice may be used for supplies between NZD 50 and NZD 1,000; tax invoices and zero-rating evidence packs must be retained for 7 years and produced to Inland Revenue on demand. E-invoicing via the Peppol network requires a Peppol ID and an access-point service contract, but remains a commercial choice rather than a statutory mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating applies where goods are exported from New Zealand under section 11(1)(a) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, with physical removal from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply and retention by the supplier of the full export documentation pack. Services (international student placement and golden visa residence advisory): zero-rating applies under section 11A(1)(a) where the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, the services are not supplied in connection with New Zealand land or goods situate in New Zealand, and the recipient does not acquire the services for personal consumption while physically present in New Zealand. Services physically rendered in New Zealand to clients present in New Zealand, and commission charges invoiced to New Zealand educational institutions, are standard-rated at 15%. The supplier must hold sufficient evidence of the recipient's non-resident status at the time of supply to sustain the zero-rating claim. The 180-day inward remittance benchmark is applied as the compliance standard for export proceeds substantiation; New Zealand legislation does not impose a separate foreign-exchange repatriation statute, and zero-rating evidence operates through the 28-day export window and the applicable GST return timelines.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Electronic Export Declaration (Tranzit/JETTR transaction set) bearing the Unique Consignment Reference (UCR) and validated export entry number
Original Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin matching the export declaration

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank-issued Foreign Exchange conversion record, including SWIFT MT103 credit advice, showing receipt of export proceeds from the offshore client in foreign currency

Offshore-client verification pack: certified copy of passport or government-issued identification, non-resident declaration, and written confirmation of the client's location outside New Zealand at the time the service was performed
Service delivery evidence: signed consulting engagement letter, placement confirmation from the New Zealand education provider, visa lodgement receipt, and dated advisory deliverables
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue operates a dedicated export zero-rating compliance program and cross-references GST returns with New Zealand Customs Service export data and banking records. Where an export claim fails substantiation (e.g., no export declaration, invoice raised after expiry of the 28-day export window, payment received from a New Zealand bank account or New Zealand-issued payment card, or evidence that the client was in New Zealand when the service was performed), the 15% GST is clawed back as output tax, together with use-of-money interest at the prescribed Inland Revenue rate (periodically reset; approximately 10.8% per annum as at 2025) and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for evasion or fraudulent intent, with criminal prosecution available under sections 143A and 143B. For the migration-advisory product line, the general anti-avoidance provisions (sections BG1 and GA1 of the Income Tax Act 2007) and the promoter-penalty regime (section 141EB of the Tax Administration Act 1994) may be invoked if the CK_IC markets or implements a zero-rating or tax-exempt structure that is artificial or lacking economic substance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the sole monetary and financial stability authority; for foreign exchange and trade, there is no separate Foreign Exchange Administration body. The Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) jointly administer the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, which governs all FX-related financial institutions and reporting entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand legally accepts its IMF Article VIII obligations, providing full convertibility on both current and capital-account transactions. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is a free-floating currency with no administrative convertibility approvals, no surrender requirements, and no distinction between current and capital account in terms of FX availability. Profit remittances from a Cook Islands International Company (IC) operating in or through New Zealand are freely transferable abroad, subject only to domestic taxation rules, including non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) or approved issuer levy (AIL) on dividends, interest, royalties, and certain service fees. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 may impose prior consent for certain capital inflows into sensitive land or significant business assets, but it does not create any FX convertibility impediment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratios, no forced delivery period, and no requirement to repatriate export or service-fee receipts into New Zealand within a prescribed timeline. A Cook Islands IC earning student placement and immigration advisory service fee income may retain its foreign currency proceeds in offshore and onshore foreign-currency accounts indefinitely, but all funds held at New Zealand registered banks are subject to AML/CFT record keeping and taxation disclosure obligations under the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2022 (as applicable).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (NZD/foreign-currency) and Client Trust Account (escrow for immigration client monies)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account; dedicated Trust Account facilities for licensed immigration advisers
Operational Account and Client Monies Trust Account (fiduciary deposit arrangement)
Operational Account only; escrow and trust services for offshore IC not standard and require special approval
Operational Account only; limited cross-border FX and escrow support, particularly for non-resident tax-exempt entities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — offshore digital electronic money institutions (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, MultiPass) are viable as supplementary payment and FX conversion rails only; they are not licensed under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 as banks and cannot provide fiduciary escrow or client trust accounts. To offer NZD-denominated services, an offshore EMI must register as a financial institution under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and appoint a New Zealand face or agent. For a Cook Islands International Company with immigration advisory activity, an EMI cannot replace an NZ-incumbent bank, because the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007 requires client funds to be held in a New Zealand trust account with a registered NZ financial institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical KYC interview is generally mandatory for at least one director and all significant beneficial owners of a Cook Islands International Company. New Zealand tier-1 banks require that a director who physically attends the bank's New Zealand branch or a designated overseas office (e.g., ANZ Singapore, HSBC Hong Kong) be verified against a valid passport and proof of residence; fully remote and digital-only onboarding will not be accepted for a tax-exempt offshore entity. Where the IC is not registered as an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993, the bank will refuse onboarding. In practice, the onboarding officer will require a New Zealand-resident director or a locally appointed authorised agent to provide a registered office and physical substance, and will mandate a face-to-face interview at an acceptable branch within 90 days of account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt Cook Islands International Company with no audited financials or physical substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Cook Islands International Company certificate of incorporation and business licence; a legal opinion from a Cook Islands counsel confirming active good standing; overseas company registration in New Zealand (Companies Office Extract under Part 18); audited or reviewed financial statements (or at minimum management accounts) covering 12 months; register of beneficial ownership with a declaration confirming that the ultimate beneficial owners are not politically exposed persons (PEPs).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No operating history or absence of a New Zealand immigration advisory licence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A copy of the New Zealand Immigration Advisers Authority (IAA) licence or a statutory exemption analysis under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007; executed commercial agreements with registered education providers (NZQA-recognised institutions) and student-clients; a detailed 12-month business plan including cash-flow projections; and a copy of the trust account rules certification from the IAA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound client funds originating from high-risk or jointly sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., China, India, Middle East, Russia, or Nigeria) for golden visa applications
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A robust source-of-funds file for each material deposit: personal income tax returns, audited business accounts, property sale records (with official registry valuation), or liquidation statements; bank account statements covering the source and the route of the funds for the preceding six months; written rationale for the visa application; evidence of the funds being held in a licensed bank in a stable jurisdiction; and negative screening against UN/EU/HM Treasury/OFAC sanctions and PEP databases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume outgoing transfers to educational institutions, recruitment agents, and government visa authorities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete fee schedule and tariff sheet; a signed disbursement mandate from each client; documentary proof that every educational institution is an approved provider under NZQA (or equally recognised in Australia, Canada, or the UK as applicable); IRD tax numbers for both the IC and the New Zealand branch; a documented anti-bribery and anti-corruption policy; and an operational matrix describing why a particular payment rail is selected for each beneficiary jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the Cook Islands IC parent to its New Zealand branch or subsidiary should be routed via SWIFT MT103 using standard purpose codes: 'TREA' for treasury operations, 'INTD' for intercompany financing, or 'SECU' for securities-related capital injection. The bank will require a board resolution, a signed capital contribution agreement, and an Overseas Investment Office (OIO) clearance letter if the funds are to be applied toward sensitive land or a significant business asset (NZ$100 million threshold) under the Overseas Investment Act 2005. For currencies such as CNY, INR, or BRL with capital-control considerations, the bank may require a deliverable or non-deliverable forward to fix the NZD cost; no repatriation restrictions apply on the equity once lawfully injected. Verification includes a notarised schedule of beneficial owners, certified tax status of the IC, and a statement demonstrating that the funds derive from legitimate commercial activity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements to educational institutions and overseas agents are normally cleared through SWIFT MT103 messages via the NZ bank's correspondent banking network. For very large transactions (above NZ$50,000) involving pre-payment of tuition or escrow release, banks offer SWIFT MT100, MT202/MT205 cover transfers, but MT103 is the standard because it carries full remitter and beneficiary details for AML/CFT screening. Where a performance or advance-payment guarantee is requested by a partner university, a commercial letter of credit (LC) may be issued under UCP 600, provided the supporting invoice, enrolment verification, and proof of insurance are presented. For jurisdictions with exchange controls (China, India), the transaction must use approved clearing rails such as CIPS (RMB) or the Bank of India–counterparty rupee route, and a non-deliverable forward (NDF) is advised to mitigate conversion risk. All outgoing settlement instructions must be validated against the SWIFT BIC database and, for account-based payments in Europe and Asia, against IBAN or national account number formats to eliminate rejection and invalid reference charges.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward (NZD vs USD, AUD, GBP, EUR, and CNY) with tenors up to 24 months
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on USD/CNY, USD/INR, and other restricted currencies to hedge tuition and commission payments
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) for long-term NZD or foreign-currency borrowings to finance educational infrastructure
FX option (call on foreign currency payable, put on NZD receivable) to produce a maximum-cost hedge while retaining upside
Vanilla currency swap executed with a licensed NZ bank where the underlying commercial exposure arises from enrolment contracts or non-resident ownership financing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a New Zealand International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due no later than the last day of the month following the entity's anniversary of incorporation, annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$4 per day up to NZ$58; continued non-compliance triggers registration removal notice and potential strike-off after 20 working days of notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within 20 working days after the due date of the Annual Return, generally aligned with incorporation anniversary month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file results in automatic registration status default and removal action; entities incur enforcement costs and strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements Filing (if audit-exempt but required under annual return obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared and filed with the Annual Return if the entity is not entitled to the audit exemption or if required by a shareholder direction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties up to NZ$4,000 for non-preparation or non-filing; directors personally liable; continued breach leads to removal from register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IRD Tax Status Annual Declaration (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return filing deadline aligned with the entity's balance date; typically 31 March for standard tax year or within 6 months of balance date for non-compliant entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of NZ$250 per month for non-filing, late payment penalties and interest; persistent failure triggers prosecution and deregistration consequences

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit required if total distributions to shareholders in the accounting period exceed NZ$100,000 in relation to a distribution of net assets; otherwise exempt unless shareholder holding 5% or more of shares directs an audit, or entity is a large overseas company with total assets exceeding NZ$60 million or revenue exceeding NZ$30 million
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) for large entities; New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) for Small and Medium-Sized Entities (NZ XRB A1 framework)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a register of shareholders and directors; any share transfer must be recorded within 10 working days. An annual confirmation of significant control and shareholding details is required via the Annual Return filing, including the names, addresses, and shareholdings of all shareholders and any ultimate holding entity. No separate UBO register is publicly filed for International Companies, but information must be retained on the statutory register and made available to regulators upon request.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not operate a general preferential corporate income tax holiday regime. The R&D Tax Incentive provides a 15% credit on eligible R&D expenditure (28% refundable for loss-making entities subject to conditions). Imputation credits (Australian-style) attach to dividends to eliminate economic double taxation on distributed profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed through the Inland Revenue myIR business gateway or approved third-party tax software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due by 7 July following the standard 31 March balance date, or within the applicable filing extension window for non-standard balance dates (e.g., 31 March balance date taxpayers with a tax agent may be extended to 31 March of the following year for payment and 31 March for filing in certain agent extension regimes). Provisional tax instalments are generally due in three instalments based on the balance date (e.g., 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May for a 31 March balance date).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / IR4 Field A (Income Tax Return – Total Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income derived in New Zealand, including worldwide income of a New Zealand tax resident company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies (including International Companies treated as non-resident for income tax purposes) must declare only New Zealand-sourced income (e.g., income from services performed in New Zealand, interest, rent, or royalty derived from New Zealand). Foreign-sourced advisory fees for offshore student placement services are excluded if the non-resident company has no New Zealand permanent establishment and no source nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / IR4 Field B (Taxable Income after Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business expenses, depreciation, and deductions allowable under the Income Tax Act 2007 (e.g., operating costs, salaries, professional fees, and administrative expenses attributable to the New Zealand activity).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct expenses to the extent they are incurred in deriving New Zealand-sourced assessable income. General overheads of a foreign head office are deductible only if directly attributable and properly apportioned, with contemporaneous documentation retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / IR4 Field C (Loss carry-forward offset)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior income years, subject to the continuity of ownership test (50% direct or indirect continuity over the loss year and the utilisation year) and the business continuity test for companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company must maintain shareholder continuity records and, if applicable, obtain Inland Revenue binding rulings when loss offset is claimed against New Zealand-sourced income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / IR4 Field D (Net tax payable after credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net company tax at 28%, after application of imputation credits (dividend withholding payment credits), tax credits for foreign income tax paid, R&D tax credits, and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are generally not entitled to imputation credits unless the imputation credit account (ICA) is maintained. Foreign tax credits may be claimed only under a New Zealand double tax agreement or the Foreign Tax Credit rules (sections LJ-LM Income Tax Act 2007) where foreign tax is paid on the same income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 for companies (escalating to NZD 500 if still outstanding after one month, with further penalties imposed at the discretion of Inland Revenue). Late payment penalty of 1% immediately on due date, then 4% at 7 days late, and 1% monthly thereafter. Use-of-money interest (currently 10.03% for underpayments and 4.03% for overpayments at standard benchmark rates, adjusted quarterly) applies on any outstanding tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory resident withholding tax (RWT) on dividends is 33% at the top marginal rate for non-resident shareholders where the dividend is not fully imputed. For dividends with full imputation credits, no further withholding is required for resident companies. Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends is 30% (reduced to 15% under the New Zealand–China DTA and generally 15% for other treaty jurisdictions with a 15% portfolio rate; 0% for a 10%+ corporate shareholder under most treaties, subject to limitation of benefits).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must complete the relevant Inland Revenue form (IR290 for NRWT reduction or approved non-resident certificate), submit a completed Certificate of Residence (Form IR290) from the jurisdiction of residence, and provide it to the New Zealand withholding agent before payment. The withholding agent applies the reduced treaty rate or zero rate only if the certificate is received and the shareholder has the beneficial ownership of the dividend. For International Companies (CK_IC) structured as a New Zealand overseas company, the DTA relief requires the shareholder to be a resident of a treaty country, not merely the IC entity; substance and beneficial ownership analysis applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties is 15% (approved issuer levy can reduce effective cost to 2% for related-party interest if the borrowing is not from a non-resident associate and the AIL election is made); statutory NRWT on interest is 15%. Treaty rates: interest generally 10% (0% for certain government/bank interest); royalties generally 5% (some treaties 10% or 10%/5% split for industrial/commercial vs literary/artistic). Under the New Zealand–China DTA, interest is 10% (0% to government-approved lenders subject to limitations), royalties are 5% for industrial, commercial or scientific equipment and 10% for other royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand TP documentation follows OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines: contemporaneous documentation is required by Inland Revenue when the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds NZD 10 million (local file master file benchmarks aligning with OECD Action 13). Master File is required where group revenue exceeds NZD 1 billion and specified transaction thresholds are met; Local File is required for transactions exceeding NZD 5 million for related-party service/sales transactions, NZD 1 million for related-party financing, and NZD 1 million for related-party IP royalty transactions. Inland Revenue's transfer pricing dispute threshold is NZD 6 million of gross income adjustment per taxpayer in relation to the dispute, and documentation must be prepared by the due date of the return.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime akin to the UAE. However, general anti-avoidance rules (BG1 Income Tax Act 2007) and the 'business test' under tax residence law require commercial substance. A CK_IC International Company claiming non-resident status must not be managed and controlled from New Zealand, must have a real foreign place of business and maintain board meetings and strategic control overseas. All arrangements must reflect economic substance (employees, premises, actual decision-making and risk assumption) to avoid being recharacterised as a New Zealand-resident company or as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing fees from study-abroad placement or golden visa advisory services, claiming fictitious deductions, or shifting profits offshore via artificial arrangements without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (evasion or similar offence, sections 143A and 143B): fine up to NZD 50,000 for individuals and NZD 250,000 for companies, plus up to 7 years imprisonment for individuals. Civil shortfall penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall for abusive tax positions, plus use-of-money interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for knowingly assisting in tax evasion, and can face personal criminal liability, pecuniary penalties, imprisonment up to 7 years, and obligation to pay the company's tax shortfall under civil penalty rules. Travel bans may be imposed where assets are dissipated or the individual is likely to leave New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a New Zealand International Company (CK_IC) that is managed and controlled from New Zealand while claiming non-resident tax status, or conducting a 'letterbox' entity with no real offices, staff, or decision-making in the claimed foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the company as a New Zealand tax resident, assessment on worldwide income at 28%, imposition of shortfall penalties up to 100-150%, loss of foreign income tax credits, and potential cancellation of registration under the Companies Act 1993 and Financial Reporting Act 2013.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit operation of a shell company with false declarations may be disqualified from managing companies under the Companies Act 1993, personally liable for unpaid tax under the tax avoidance recovery provisions, and subject to criminal penalties for false declarations to Inland Revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML/CFT) and Unlicensed Immigration Advice
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing immigration/visa placement services without holding a New Zealand Immigration Advisers Authority (IAA) license or exemption, or failing to comply with AML/CFT obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, including accepting wire transfer payments without customer due diligence, or facilitating visa fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007: a fine of up to NZD 100,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 7 years for unlicensed immigration advice. AML/CFT penalties: civil penalties up to NZD 2 million for the body corporate for each contravention, and criminal fines up to NZD 400,000; Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) must be filed and a compliance officer appointed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers can be prosecuted personally under the AML/CFT Act (individual liability up to NZD 200,000 fine and/or imprisonment), subject to personal pecuniary penalties, orders for civil restitution, travel bans in connection with criminal proceedings, and disqualification from immigration advisory practice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Cross-Border Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for related-party fees, mispricing intra-group management fees or royalty payments, or stripping New Zealand profits through excessive interest deductions falling within the non-resident interest limitation rules (NRIL) applicable to 40% of an entity's net debt (limiting interest deductibility where the ratio exceeds 40% for non-resident related-party debt).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable income under s GC8 Income Tax Act 2007, applying the arm's length standard with penalties up to 150% for transfer pricing adjustments or documentation failure. Interest limitation rules may disallow interest deductions entirely for certain excessive related-party debt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign transfer pricing documentation that is false or misleading can face penalties for aiding and abetting, personal liability for the shortfall penalty, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion, including imprisonment up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Profit Repatriation and Dividend Withholding Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to non-resident shareholders through untaxed 'interest-free loans', or mischaracterising dividends as management fees or repayments of capital to avoid NRWT, or failing to file the Resident Withholding Tax (RWT) declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A non-resident withholding tax deficiency is assessed at the statutory 30% dividend rate (or 15% interest/royalty rate) plus penalty tax of 150% for evasion and use-of-money interest. A company that fails to withhold NRWT is jointly and severally liable for the tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under the Companies Act for causing the company to distribute assets where the company is insolvent or where the distribution is made without regard to tax obligations; personal liability for NRWT arises as the withholding agent; criminal liability applies for knowingly evading withholding tax (fines up to NZD 250,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years).
